question.leadin: The Treaty of Zaragoza increased the scope of this treaty in 1529.
question.text: Name this treaty that created a line of demarcation 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, allowing Portugal to colonize the land east of the line and Spain the land to the west.
question.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

swap.text: Soldiers and explorers of the New World like Cortes and his men are often known by this Spanish word that translates to "conqueror."
swap.clue: One of these people wrote a "true history" that recounts how another of them wept during a 1520 event which translates to "The Sad Night."

question.text: Merged with the Carlists by Franco, this Spanish fascist movement was founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera.
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.leadin: In 1099, Valencian soldiers scared away Almoravid invaders by placing this leader's body on his horse Bavieca, making it appear he had returned from the dead.
swap.text: Name this legendary Spanish warrior, a mercenary who fought on behalf of the Emir of Zaragoza against King Alfonso XI of Castile before claiming Valencia as his own.
swap.answerHtml: El Cid [or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; prompt on Díaz alone; or El Campeador or the Champion, or Le Cid]
swap.clue: This ruler of Valencia who fought both for and against the Taifa of Zargoza.

question.text: Following Mary I's death, Phillip sent this force to overthrow Elizabeth I in 1588.
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.text: The Ebro flows into the Mediterranean at Tarragona, a city in this autonomous community of Spain which has its capital at Barcelona.
swap.clue: That one saw the loss of the Rousillon and Cerdagne, which were northern portions of this region.

question.leadin: Louis XIV got France into a lot of wars.
question.text: Louis's last war, this conflict was precipitated by the death of Charles II, and saw the end of French hegemony in Europe. It was concluded with the Treaty of Utrecht.
question.clue: Other battles in this conflict include one in which Marshall Villars clashed with Eugene of Savoy at Malplaquet, and Marlborough aided Prince Leopold's armies against Louis XIV at Blenheim.

swap.text: The fall of this city in the Andalusian region marked the end of Muslim rule in Spain.
swap.clue: Following his honeymoon with Isabella of Portugal, Charles V had a palace constructed by Diego Machuca within the walls of this city's most famous structure.

question.leadin: Give these terms from the rule of Napoleon.
question.text: Known as War of Independence by native Spaniards, this attempt to subjugate Portugal and Spain lasted from 1808 to 1814.

swap.text: The physician Abu al-Qasim did pioneering work on dissections and removing bladder stones in this city. Abd ar-Rahman III ruled from this city, whose massive Great Mosque contained a Court of the Oranges and was converted to a Catholic cathedral in 1236.
swap.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

question.leadin: This group declared a ceasefire in September 2010 after an earlier, broken "permanent ceasefire" in 2006.
question.text: Name this group responsible for assassinating Prime Minister Luis Carrero Blanco in 1973 and accused by some of carrying out some 2004 train bombings in a capital city.
question.clue: This group's political wing was the Herri Batasuna.

swap.leadin: This campaign began with the founding of the kingdom of Asturias following its victory at Covadonga.
swap.text: Name this centuries long movement during which Christian kingdoms attempted to reconquer the Iberian Peninsula from Muslim forces.
swap.clue: During this period, a coalition of Christian knights joined together to defeat Muhammad al-Nasir at the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa.

question.leadin: A descendant of the Duchy of Vascony, its southern part was eventually absorbed by Castille.
question.text: Identify this kingdom spanning the Pyrenees ruled by kings like Sancho the Great, which had its capital at Pamplona and once shared its name with that city.
question.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

swap.text: This legendary Spanish warrior and Castilian national hero served Sancho II and later became the ruler of Valencia. He's memorialized by a lengthy "Cantar" [kahn-TAR], as well as a Pierre Corneille play.
swap.answerHtml: El Cid Campeador [or El Cid Campeador; or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; accept Le Cid; prompt on Díaz]
swap.clue: After his recall he fought off Tashafin's army, which had responded to pleas from local lords by forcing the Battle of az-Zallaqah, a massive Almoravid victory.

question.text: Castilian king Ferdinand's Alhambra Decree, which expelled the Jews from Spain and allowed Muslims to stay, was signed after a battle which ended the Iberian Reconquista by conquering this last Muslim kingdom.
question.clue: A fortified complex in this polity's namesake city was beautified by Yusuf I, whose successor built the Court of the Lions.

swap.leadin: Name some things related to everyone's favorite medieval manuscript, the Liber feudorum maior.
swap.text: The Liber feudorum maior was commissioned by Alfonso II from this state. Under Ferdinand II of this state, it combined with Castile, which was led by Isabella.
swap.clue: Pope Martin IV ("the fourth") ordered a crusade against this kingdom after its ruler Peter III ("the third") accepted a request to invade Sicily in response to the Sicilian Vespers.

question.leadin: It succeeded the Kingdom of Asturias after Ordono II moved the capital from Oviedo.
question.text: Name this Spanish kingdom united with Castile under Ferdinand III.
question.clue: In a now-discredited theory, the founding of this kingdom was part of a "repopulation" of the "Desert of the Duero."

swap.text: This conservative Spanish prime minister switched places with Liberal Praxedes Mateo Sagasta during the turno pacifico. His support of the Carlists led to his 1897 assassination by Italian anarchist Michel Angiolillo.

question.text: This Spanish church doctor also railed against the Jews in On the Catholic Faith Against the Jews and maintained that the Earth was round in an encyclopedia entitled Etymologiae or Origins.
question.answerHtml: Saint Isidore of Seville [or San Isidro or San Isidoro de Sevilla; do NOT accept "San Isidro Labrador"]
question.clue: This man's younger sister Florentina allegedly held claim over forty convents, and at her request he wrote his two books Against the Jews, while his younger brother Fulgentius served as bishop of Astigi.

swap.leadin: Spain had a famous some Restoration periods too. Answer the following about one of them, FTPE.
swap.text: After the brief experiment of the First Republic, this Bourbon son of Isabella II was given the throne in 1874, establishing a constitutional monarchy in its place.
swap.clue: This man, who spent part of his time in exile attending Sandhurst College, returned to Spain and was proclaimed king following the overthrow of the First Spanish Republic. Antonio Canovas de Castillo promulgated the royalist constitution during this monarch's reign in 1876.
